payload.say: Every animal has to find food. A goat eats grass, a tiger eats the goat. But a plant never goes anywhere. So where does a plant get its food from? It makes its own.

payload.say: A leaf needs three things. Sunlight from above, water pulled up from the roots, and a gas from the air called carbon dioxide. Put those three together and the leaf can build food.

payload.say: Inside every leaf there is a green colour called chlorophyll. That green is what catches the sunlight. No chlorophyll, no catching sunlight, no food. That is why almost every leaf you have ever seen is green.

payload.say: The leaf keeps the food it makes, and it lets out oxygen. That is the gas we breathe. So the tree outside your classroom is quietly making the air you are breathing right now.

payload.say: Have you ever talked to Siri or used Google Maps? Those tools use a kind of computer thinking called artificial intelligence. AI helps machines understand what we say and find the best answer. It is like a smart helper that works all the time.

payload.say: Artificial intelligence means making a machine think like a human. It does not have a brain, but it can learn from many examples. The machine looks at patterns and then makes predictions. This learning is called machine learning.

payload.say: Imagine showing a computer thousands of pictures of cats and dogs. The computer notices differences and remembers them. Later, when it sees a new picture, it can say whether it is a cat or a dog. This is how AI can recognize objects.

payload.say: There are two kinds of AI. Narrow AI works for one job, like recommending songs. General AI would do many tasks like a human, but we do not have it yet. Most AI today is narrow and very useful.
